To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the seroprevelance of hepatitis E virus (26.7 %) differs in Dutch and in migrant populations in Amsterdam.

HEV seroprevlance is high among first generation migrants from Morocco, lower among first generation migrants of other ethnicities, and lowest among first generation migrants originating from Turkey, compared to the Dutch population.
HEV seropositives in the Dutch participants had a higher median age than HEV seronegatives, while in first generation migrants from Morocco this was not the case.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the epidemiology of HEV in the Netherlands and in particular in migrant communities.
the role of migration in HEV transmission.
the role of migrants in the epidemiology of HEV in developed countries and shows that the HEV serology of migrants is an important tool in understanding HEV epidemiology in developed countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HEV sero-epidemiology of Amsterdam migrants is complex.
the HEV sero-epidemiology in the migrant populations in Amsterdam is different from that of the autochthon population and that this difference is mainly explained by the country of origin.
there is a difference in HEV seropositives between different ethnic groups and the autochthonic population in Amsterdam.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HEV seropositivities in first generation migrant groups were not only determined by their country of birth but also by their age at time of immigration and their age at time when they were tested.
the HEV seroepidemiology in migrants in the Netherlands differs from that of the autochthon Dutch population.
the HEV prevalence in the Netherlands is high in the Moroccan and lower in the other migrant populations and that the Dutch population has an intermediate prevalence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HEV seropositives are found among first generation migrants in Amsterdam, but that this is not a uniform phenomenon.
HEV serology is important to include in serological surveys among migrants in Europe.
HEV seropositives should be screened for HEV RNA in order to detect chronic HEV infection.
